title: Te Whakamātautau a te Mea Tapu
intro: I tukuna he tohu ki tētahi iwi kua hē. I waenganui i ō rātou oranga whakamarie ka puta mai he whakatūpato—me tētahi mea whakamiharo i haere tahi me ia hei whakamātautau whakamutunga mō tō rātou whakapono. Mā tā rātou urupare e hiri tō rātou aituā ake ake. Ka taea e koe te hura ko wai i tuku i tēnei whakatūpato, ā, i pēhea te hunga i whakakahore?
clues: He iwi tātou i arahina e ngā karere o mua i mua i a tātou.
I puta mai tētahi mea whakamiharo i te maunga, he tohu nā tō tātou Ariki mō tēnei iwi.
I mea atu ahau ki a rātou: 'He kamera uha tēnei nā Allah, nō reira waiho kia kai ia i te oneone a Allah, kaua hoki e pā ki a ia.'
Heoi i whakangote te iwi i taku kamera uha, i te whakakeketanga ki te whakahau a to ratou Ariki.
He karere noa iho ahau nā tōu Ariki, i tonoa mai me te pono—he poropiti pono, he pononga hoki ahau.
Mō te hunga hara, i pāngia rātou e tō tātou Ariki ki te haruru nui, ā, ka noho korekore noa iho rātou i roto i ō rātou kāinga.

arabic: إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ فَكَانُوا۟ كَهَشِيمِ ٱلْمُحْتَظِرِ
verse: Indeed, We sent upon them one shriek [i.e., blast from the sky], and they became like the dry twig fragments of an [animal] pen. (54:31)
